case_title: Ram Saran Varshney v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_occupation: Director (husband, as described in the second closure report; not a Court finding)
accused_socioeconomic_status: Husband described as son of an IAS officer (closure report statement; not a Court finding)
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband); in-laws (parents-in-law and sisters-in-law) are relatives by marriage; marital discord and divorce petition filed by husband
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498A, s.506; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.4
evidence_type: Investigation statements of complainant and family members, case diary; no trial evidence discussed by the Court
confession: None relied on by the Court; the third closure report records an alleged admission (email) by the complainant, which was not accepted by the Court
trial_court_outcome: No verdict; cognizance of charge sheet taken on 12.5.2008 and accused summoned to face trial; trial pending
high_court_outcome: Petition under s.482 CrPC seeking quashing of charge sheet and orders dismissed (1.12.2008)
neutral_facts: The complainant, the wife of one of the accused, lodged a first information report alleging that her husband, his parents and his sisters harassed her in connection with dowry. She alleged that a demand of Rs 10 lakh had been made and that she would be harassed and tortured if it was not met. The couple had a daughter born in 2000 and lived together in Pune until October 2001, when the complainant left the matrimonial home. In March 2002 she attempted to enter her parents-in-law's house in Lucknow. A first investigating officer filed a closure report finding no substance in the allegations and attributing the dispute to personal differences. On the complainant's protest, further investigation was ordered, and a second officer again recommended closure, noting that the dowry demand rested only on oral statements without independent evidence. A third officer's closure report stated that the complainant had written an email claiming dowry had been demanded, and recorded that maintenance and a bank draft had been provided. Later, a fourth officer, carrying out investigation after the earlier reports, filed a charge sheet under the cruelty and dowry provisions against the husband, his parents and his sisters. The complainant's family was described in the reports as well-to-do; no independent witness to the alleged demand was identified in the earlier reports.
number_of_offences: 4 charged (IPC s.498A, s.506; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.4); 0 finally upheld (no conviction; trial pending)
financial_property_loss: Not applicable (alleged dowry demand of Rs 10 lakh; no loss found by the Court)
motive: alleged: dowry demand of Rs 10 lakh; the Court did not decide the motive
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence on the merits was assessed; the Court accepted that the second closure report was considered by the Magistrate and that the third closure report was a nullity
witness_credibility: Not assessed on merits; no trial evidence was considered
bail_history: Arrest stayed by High Court (Writ Petition (MB) No. 2600 of 2002); no bail order stated
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR registered 10.04.2002); trial judgment: not given (cognizance order 12.05.2008); High Court: 01.12.2008; Supreme Court: 05.02.2016
legal_representation: Appellants: Huzefa Ahmadi, M. Shoeb Alam, Shahrukh Alam, Rohan, Ujjwal Singh. Respondent no.2: Pawan Shree Aggarwal, Pragati Neekhra; Sonia Gupta in person. State of UP: learned counsel (name not stated)
investigation_status: FIR registered 10.04.2002; first, second and third closure reports (27.4.2003, 10.07.2003, 27.02.2007); fourth investigating officer filed charge sheet 7.5.2008; cognizance taken 12.5.2008
procedural_irregularity: Third closure report was prepared during a stay of the further-investigation order and held a nullity; further investigation carried out without a fresh court direction after the third closure report
appeal_history: Trial court: cognizance and summons 12.5.2008; Sessions Court revision dismissed 1.7.2008; High Court s.482 petition dismissed 1.12.2008; Supreme Court: disposed of, quashed against appellant nos. 4-6, proceedings against appellant nos. 1-3 to continue
prosecution_argument: Second closure report was deemed considered when further investigation was ordered on 6.9.2006; third closure report was based on a valid order and the earlier reports were considered
defence_argument: Charge sheet and cognizance order were cryptic and ignored the second and third closure reports; appellant nos. 4-6 had no concern with the marital relationship and no clear allegations were made against them
legal_principle_applied: Magistrate's further-investigation power exercised sparingly; investigation in violation of an express judicial order is a nullity; proceedings against relatives quashed where no specific allegations or material of harassment exist
precedent_relied_upon: Vinay Tyagi vs. Irshad Ali alias Deepak and others, (2013) 5 SCC 762
other_sentence_order: Trial court requested to dispose of proceedings against appellant nos. 1 to 3 as expeditiously as possible; proceedings against appellant nos. 4, 5 and 6 quashed
